The petitioner has filed petition U/s. 22 of the Employee's Compensation Act, claiming compensation from the respondents, for the injuries sustained by him, during the course of his employment under the first respondent.
2. The petition averments in brief are as under:
The petitioner submits that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the Eicher Mahindra Canter Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-52-B-5152 and the petitioner was working as as a driver of the said goods vehicle.

It is alleged that on 17.05.2023 at about 01.45 a.m., when the petitioner was on his work and driving the Mahindra Eicher Canter Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-52-B- 5152 near Anesidri village, in front of Nanda Feeds Factory, Bengaluru towards Chitradurga NH-4 main, at about 1.45 a.m, the petitioner has lost control over the vehicle and dashed against the back side of Lorry bearing Reg. No.TN-52-U-5666.
Due to the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
In this regard the FIR has came to be registered in Hiriyuru Rural Police Station in Crime No.201/2023.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Hiriyuru wherein he took first aid treatment and later he was shifted to THS Super speciality Hospital, Tumkuru for further treatment.

In this regard the petitioner claiming the compensation Rs.15,00,000/- towards hospitalization charges, treatment medicines,
conveyance, nourishing food and other incidental charges etc.,

Prior to the accident,
petitioner was very hale and healthy and he was working as Driver under respondent No.1 and getting income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries petitioner is not able to continue his work and is under complete bed rest and he is suffering from permanent disability.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Hence,
prays to award compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- with interest as reasonable compensation.
3. After service of notices, both the respondents appeared and filed their respective written statements.
First respondent admits that the petitioner was proceeding as driver in a eicher canter vehicle and also admitted that the alleged accident.
The income of the petitioner as alleged in the petition is also admitted by the respondent No.1.
Further contended that the said vehicle was insured with second respondent and the driver of the said vehicle had valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.1 prays to dismiss the petition against him.

The respondent No.2 insurance company in the written statement admitted the issuance of policy to the eicher canter bearing Reg.No. KA-52-B-5152 and the liability of this respondent if any, is subjected to the terms and condition of the insurance policy.
Further contended that, the respondent No.1 knowing fully well that, the driver did not possess valid and effective driving license and willfully entrusted the vehicle to the said driver.
Further denied the age, avocation, relationship of the employer and employee between the petitioner and respondent No.1 and income of the petitioner.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.

Hence,
the respondent No.2 prays to dismiss the petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival contention, the following issues are framed by this court:
1.
Whether the petitioner proves that, he was an employee under respondent No.1?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injury during the course of employment under the respondent No.1?
3. Whether petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injury on 17.05.2023 during the course of employment under the respondent No.1?

4. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate and from whom?
5. What Order or Award?

The petitioner has examined Dr. Ramesh as PW.2, through him Ex.P16 &
17 documents are marked.
One Jaya Kumar, who is working as Medical Records Officer at Tumkur Hospital is examined as PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P18 & 19.
The petitioner has also examined Dr. Krishna Prasad as PW.4, through him Ex.P20 document is marked.
The respondents have not lead any rebuttal evidence.
6. I have heard the arguments of both sides and perused the material evidence that are available on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under.

9. The petitioner to prove his claim have produced true copies of FIR, complaint, spot mahazar along with sketch, wound certificate, IMV report and charge sheet, which are marked under Ex.P.1 to 15.
10.
The Ex.P1 to P7 are belongs to the documents of Crime No.201-2023 of Hiriyur Rural P.S.

The petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and filed evidence affidavit which is in consonance with the contents of petition wherein he alleged that while he was driving eicher canter bearing Reg.No.
KA-52-B-5152, caused the accident from which, he got injured.

11. In the same manner, the respondent No.1 who is the owner of the eicher canter bearing Reg.No.
KA-52- B-5152 also filed written statement and wherein he also admitted that the petitioner who was a driver in eicher canter bearing Reg.No. KA-52-B-5152 and also admitted the fact of accident.
Both the petitioner and respondent No.1 have not produced any documents to establish their employer and employee relationship except ExP.8 salary slips.

At the time of cross-examination the PW.1 answered that he has no documents to produce to establish the employer and employee relationship between himself and the respondent No.1 except Ex.P.8 salary slips.
At the time of cross-examination PW.1 answered that he was working from past one year to accident in the respondent No.1 company as driver.
In this regard if we perused Ex.P.1 FIR and Ex.P.2 which is given to the jurisdictional police on 17.05.2023 at about 9.00 a.m. by reporting the fact of accident.
In Ex.P.2 itself it is stated that one Sateesha was driving Lorry bearing No.KA-52-B-5152 and caused the accident and also got injuries to his forehead, lips, chest and legs.
On the basis of Ex.P.2 Ex.P.1 was registered wherein Satish i.e., the petitioner of this case was shown as the driver of Lorry bearing No.KA-52-B-5152.
The FIR was registered soon after the accident within 8 hours of the accident.
In the said Ex.P.2 and Ex.P.1 it is clearly mentioned the said Satisha i.e., the petitioner of this petition as driver.

No grounds are made out to show the collusion or to disbelieve the contents of Ex.P.1 and P2.
12.

The petitioner even though not produced any other independent documents to establish that he is a employee under respondent No.1 his oral evidence has to be looked into along with the other documents produced by the petitioner.
Ex.P1 FIR is came to be registered on 17.05.2023 on the basis of complaint given by the respondent No.1.

In the Ex.P2 the informant informed about the alleged accident and also by alleging the rash and negligent driving by the driver of KA-52-B-5152 and also injury to the driver of the eicher canter bearing Reg.No. KA-52-B-5152.

In the Ex.P2 the informant informed the police about the injuries to the driver of eicher canter bearing Reg.No.
KA-52-B-5152.
Further the Ex.P4 spot mahazar also established the nature of the alleged accident.
The Ex.P6 IMV report also depicts the nature of damages found on the vehicles involved in the accident.
Ex.P7 is the head of the charge sheet in which the respondent No.1 is shown as owner and the petitioner as driver of the vehicle bearing No.KA-52-B-5152.
The Ex.P5 is the wound certificate which also supported the case of the petitioner about the alleged accident and injuries.
Ex.P9 copy of discharge summary depicts the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner.

The police documents established the fact of accident.

The Ex.P2 first information which is lodged by the person who is not connected with the petitioner or respondent No.1 has described the petitioner as a driver of eicher canter bearing Reg.No. KA-52-B-5152.

The respondent No.1 who is the owner of eicher canter bearing No. KA-52-B- 5152 appeared and admitted that the petitioner was working as a driver in eicher canter bearing Reg.No. KA- 52-B-5152.
14.

By considering all these points, issue No.1 to 3, answered in the affirmative by holding that the petitioner is an employee under respondent No.1 and he has sustained grievous injury during the course of employment under the respondent No.1.

Issue No.4:
15.

The petitioner to prove that he has taken treatment as inpatient has examined one Jaya Kumar,
Medical Record Officer at THS Super Speciality Hospital, Tumkur, as PW.3 through him case sheet and X-ray which are marked at Ex.P18 & 19.
These documents shows that the petitioner has taken treatment in THS Super Speciality Hospital, Tumkur as inpatient.
16. Dr.Ramesh Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, as PW.2, through him OPD book and X-ray are marked under Ex.P.16 & 17.
According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained right tibia fracture.
Further PW.2 deposed that, total disability of the right lower limb at 28% and whole body physical disability at 14%.
17. Further the petitioner has also examined Dr. Krishna Prasad A.H. Eye surgeon at Srikara Eye Clinic, Bengaluru as PW.4 through him OPD card is marked under Ex.P20.

According to the evidence of this witness the petitioner sustained loss of vision in left eye and he was treated for left eye cornea scleral laceration, left eyebrow, left upper eyelid laceration and other injuries.
As per case sheet eyelid, eyebrow, cornea scleral laceration repair was done on 17.05.2023.
Further PW.4 deposed that, total visual disability at 30%.
18. According to the evidence of PW.2, the petitioner needs one more surgery for removal of implants, but he has not estimated the cost..
This aspect is not impeached during the course of cross-examination.
It is also not the case of the respondents that, implant is removed.
Hence, it can be considered that the petitioner is required at least Rs.30,000/- for future medical expenses.
19. It is already held that the petitioner is an employee under respondent No.1 and he has sustained grievous injury during the course of employment under the respondent No.1.
As per wound certificate marked at Ex.P5 the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner further stated that after the accident he is not able to continue with his avocation and he has sustained permanent disability.

20. To prove the fact of disability the petitioner examined two doctors i.e., PW.2 Orthopedician wherein he assessed the particular limb disability for right tibia fracture at 28% and for whole body Satheesha S vs Sri Nandi Enterprises on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4310246/

sentences.text: The Ex.P.9 discharge summary of THS Super Speciality hospital discloses that the petitioner sustained injury to his face and also right lower limb due to the accident.
In the said hospital as per Ex.P.9 the petitioner was diagnosed for right tibia fracture and total laceration of frontal side eyebrow, upper and lower eyelid.
For the injuries to the eye as per Ex.P.5 wound certificate and Ex.P.9 discharge summary the Suturing was done for eyelid laceration.
21. The PW.4 is an eye surgeon who assessed the disability and on clinical examination he has found that the petitioner has lost left eye vision totally and the said visual loss is irreversible.

PW.4 eye surgeon also stated that because of loss of vision in left eye due to restricted field of vision, loss of death perception the petitioner has the difficulty to drive vehicle because of loss of binocular vision.
PW.4 eye surgeon assessed the visual disability at 30% as per the guidelines.
22. Thereby, there are two disability assessments are available on record.
The expert evidence adduced by the PW.2 orthopedician and PW.4 eye surgeon is not impeached by the respondent No.2 and no other expert evidence is adduced by the respondent No.2.

23. Coming to the fact of quantum of compensation is concerned, the petitioner deposed that he was getting the salary of Rs.20,000/- from the respondent No.1 by working as driver in eicher canter bearing No. KA-52-B-5152.
Even though the employer and employee relationship is established, the quantum of income of the petitioner is not established.
24. The petitioner produced Ex.P10- copy of DL in which, the date of birth of the petitioner is 9.4.1993.
No other documents or evidence is available on the side of both parties to consider the age of the petitioner.
Hence, by relying on Ex.P10, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident is 30 years.
According to the Petitioner he was drawing salary of Rs.20,000/- per month.
To substantiate this contention he has produced salary slips at Ex.P.8, but not adduced any account statement.
As per Ex.P.8 salary slip in the month of January and March-2023 the petitioner was getting the salary of Rs.18,478/-.
The same is considered as the income of the petitioner.

25. The doctor examined as PW.2 and 4 and assessed the disability of the petitioner at 14% and 30%
respectively.
Under Sec. 4 of Employees Compensation Act, the provision is made to calculate the amount of compensation.
The injuries sustained by the petitioner in respect of right tibia is not coming under the part I Or II of the Schedule I of the Employees Compensation Act.

sentences.text: But the injury to eye and loss of eye vision in the left side is coming under the Sl.No.26 Part-II of Schedule-I of the Employees Compensation Act.

When there is multiple injuries, explanation- I to Sec. 4 of the Employees Compensation Act is applicable and it states as follows:
4. Amount of compensation.- (1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the amount of compensation shall be as follows, namely:--
(c) where permanent partial disablement result from the injury:
(i) in the case of an injury specified in Part II of Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation which would have been payable in the case of permanent total Satheesha S vs Sri Nandi Enterprises on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4310246/
6 disablement as is specified therein as being the percentage of the loss of earning capacity caused by that injury; and (ii) in the case of an injury not specified in Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning capacity (as assessed by the qualified medical practitioner)
permanently caused by the injury;
Explanation I.--Where more injuries than one are caused by the same accident, the amount of compensation payable under this head shall be aggregated but not so in any case as to exceed the amount which would have been payable if permanent total disablement had resulted from the injuries.
Explanation II.--In assessing the loss of earning capacity for the purpose of sub-clause (ii), the qualified medical practitioner shall have due regard to the percentages of loss of earning capacity in relation to different injuries specified in Schedule I;

sentences.text: In this case, as the injuries sustained by the petitioner in respect of right tibia is not mentioned in Schedule I as such the evidence of the doctor is plays very important role.
As there is multiple injuries i.e., injury to right tibia and loss of vision in left eye by applying the Explanation- I to Sec.4 the aggregate disability has to be considered.
In respect of loss of eye vision the Act is clear that the 30% of the disability has to be considered and no reduction can be done in respect of this disability.
For a driver right leg plays very much important as such the disability in respect of right leg is considered at 10%, thereby the total disability is considered at 40%.

As discussed above, by considering the assessment given by the doctors, in comparison with the avocation of the petitioner,
the loss of the earning capacity is taken at 40%.
As per section 4 of Employees Compensation Act while deciding the loss of income of an employee the court has to decide the relevant factor based on the age of the Petitioner.
As mentioned above the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident was 30 years.
The relevant factor given to his age in schedule 4 of the act is 207.98.
As per section 4(1)(b), 60% of his monthly wages has to be multiplied by relevant factor.
The 60% of the total salary of the Petitioner is Rs.11,092/- (Rs.18,487/- x 60% =Rs.11,092/-) and it has to be multiplied by having reference to the percentage of disability and relevant factor.
Therefore the Petitioner in total is entitled for a sum of Rs.9,22,765/-.
under the head of loss of future earnings/income.
27. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The bills produced by the petitioner is marked at Ex.P11.
The Ex.P11 supported with Ex.P.12 prescriptions.
He has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.9 which evidentiates that he took treatment as inpatient at THS Super speciality Hospital from 17.05.2023 to 24.05.2023.
By considering the same, the petitioner is entitle for reimbursement of the medical bills spent by him which are marked at Ex.P11.

Medical Expenses Rs.2,04,605-00 3. Future Medical Expenses Rs. 30,000-00 Total Rs.11,57,370-00 Liability:
28.
Admittedly the respondent No.1 and 2 are the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 in its objection statement admitted issuance of policy to the eicher canter bearing Reg. No. KA-51-B-5152.

Hence, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner and the respondent No.2 insurance company shall indemnify the compensation on behalf of the respondent No.1.
The petitioner is entitle for compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.

ISSUE NO.5:
29.

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 22 of Employees Compensation Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.11,57,370/- (Rupees Eleven lakhs fifty seven thousand three hundred seventy only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
It is further clarified that the compensation awarded under the head of future medical expenses shall not carry any interest.

Out of total compensation awarded to the Petitioner, 50% shall be released in favour the petitioner on his proper identification and remaining 50% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank, for a period of three years, in his name.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.

O RDE R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 22 of Employees Compensation Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
